newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds buoyant but not ready for big leap today.
newsitem.headline: Bunds buoyant but not ready for big leap today.

text.p: German Bunds edged higher in early trade on Monday as sentiment remained positive but dealers said the market was unlikely to make a major leap forward ahead of U.S. data due later this week.
September Bund futures were rading at 103.03 at 0730 GMT, up four basis points from Friday's close, after rising as high as 103.13, just short of the contract high of 103.15.

Trading was quiet due to the closure of the French market for the Bastille Day holiday. "The market still looks to be in relatively good condition, we may see Bunds testing the contract high and briefly touching 103.20," one dealer said.
"I don't think people are going to want to lean too far out of the window."
This week sees a string of data including U.S. June retail sales on Tuesday, followed on Wednesday by U.S. consumer prices, industrial production and business inventories.
German M3 money supply for June is expected to be released at the end of this week or early next. The Ifo business climate index for June will be released on Friday at 0800 GMT.
Dealers said the market's rapid recovery from declines last week demonstrated its resilience and proved that market sentiment remained bullish.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell wrote in a note to investors that the trend was bullish due to weak domestic consumer spending and investment, the possibility that there will be no further 10-year bond issues this year, and a wealth of cash waiting on the sidelines to be invested.
The Ifo business climate index was expected to rise to 95.8 from 95.3 but its market impact was likely to be slight.

"As much as traders and investors pay attention to this report the trend of the IFO really has shown a poor correlation with the direction of the German bond market this year," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.
"The current mix of economic growth simply puts no upward pressure on interest rates,"
